title: Leads on the Move

intro.quote: “Honestly the lead listing is too good but anything with the too heavy data is not pure responsive.” — and Q-08 of the Contracts page: the next module is Leads.
intro.method: A read-only audit of every Leads screen at 390 (phone), 768 (tablet, portrait) and 1024 (tablet, landscape) with touch emulation, on a production build of main after Quotes and Contracts on the move (a6caecb1). Three lanes measured touch boxes, type sizes and taps-to-finish, read the code behind each screen, and moved their own test leads from New to Won on a scratch database. Nothing of the proposal is built. Two blockers were plain bugs and are fixed tonight; they need no pick.
answer: The listing stays — it is the benchmark — and gains the two lines that decide the next call: when we last spoke and what is next. Everything after the listing changes shape on a phone: a lead opens as a person and a position (the stage and its days, Call and WhatsApp as buttons, one Next line, what is due now, a row per tab), with a sticky foot that holds Log ▾ and the next move. Logging a call becomes three taps after the call; the Move stage window becomes one step per screen; a new lead is a name and a mobile.

This reuses what Quotes and Contracts built this week — the screen with a hero and a Next line, the rows that open as screens, the sticky foot, the tablet column sets, Take a photo · Choose a file. What is genuinely new for a lead is the capture after a call or a visit, and the Next line built from the stage and the earliest follow-up.

proposalTitle: The proposal: a lead is a person and a position; its moments are captures
proposalIntro: Six rules, then the screens drawn with OpenMaison’s own tokens, then each change as a card you can mark. Desktop stays exactly as it is; the stage rules, the logs and the records are the same code behind a different order of screens.

principles.title: Who to call now, first
principles.body: The card and the lead both lead with the next call: when we last spoke, what is next, how late it is. Everything else is one tap further.

principles.title: One primary per screen
principles.body: The filled button is the next move (Move to Met, Convert to Project, Resume at …). Logging sits beside it as Log ▾. Everything else is behind ⋮.

principles.title: A moment is a capture
principles.body: A call, a visit, a photo: captured in three taps with now already set, the outcome as chips and the photo from the camera.

principles.title: One thing at a time
principles.body: A tab opens as its own screen; a stage step is one screen with "step n of 5". No sideways strips, no rails.

principles.title: Nothing typed is lost
principles.body: A refusal says why before you type, or stays in the foot after; ✕ asks before it discards.

principles.title: A tablet is not a small desktop
principles.body: Upright it follows the phone; sideways it holds the person beside the open tab. Tables show the columns a finger needs.

proposals.title: A lead opens as a person and a position on a phone
proposals.today: The Overview is the desktop’s three columns stacked: the name twice, a static header whose stage pill and "Move to …" scroll away, the brief at 43% of the first screen, LEAD STAGES a screen down, cards at 12px, empty cards a quarter of the page; Call is a 70×20 link beside two 24px glyphs.
proposals.proposed: The Lead screen (the Quote / Contract screen’s frame): a 56 bar (← · the name over "Contacted · 4 days" · ⋮ with Create first); a hero (the stage chip and its days, property · budget · source, the address with Directions, the client row with Call and WhatsApp as 44 buttons); one Next line from a new pure lib/leads/next-step.ts — the stage and the earliest open follow-up ("Call back — Thu 10:00 is overdue", "Assign a member — Sarah has room", "Sent 4 days ago · not opened"), the brief one line under it; Due now (at most three overdue / today tasks with a 44 ring); a row per tab with its count and next thing; a sticky foot with Log ▾ (Call · WhatsApp · Visit · Note) and the next move. Signed / Won: Open project.
proposals.why: the person on site wants the client’s number, what is late and the next move in one look. The pieces exist since this week; the hero’s contents and the Next line are what is new.

proposals.title: A tab opens as its own screen on a phone
proposals.today: Every tab repeats the name, the stage row and a sideways strip of nine tabs (4½ visible) before its toolbar: 241px of chrome; Notes & Logs, Meetings, Questionnaire and Activity are off-screen with no cue.
proposals.proposed: On a phone the tabs are the Lead screen’s rows; a row opens its tab as a screen with a 56 bar (← · "Tasks" over "Farah Ahmad" · the tab’s + and ⋮), the body, no strip. The address stays the tab’s (Back returns to the lead). The stage row on each tab is your REG-370 decision — see Q-04.
proposals.why: one thing at a time; 241px of chrome on every tab is the cost of carrying the desktop’s frame.

proposals.title: Log a call in three taps, from the lead or from Notes
proposals.today: A first call is 13 taps and a mandatory screenshot in the Move stage window, 8–10 from Notes: the date opens empty although it is being written now, the outcome is a list behind a select, the attach sheet says "Drop your file or browse" and has no camera.
proposals.proposed: After a press on Call or WhatsApp, the Lead screen offers Log the call (Q-06); the sheet has the channel and now set, the five outcomes as chips, a call-back with presets (Tomorrow 10:00 · In 3 days · Next week), an optional photo (Take a photo first) and one Save log. On a New lead Save logs it and moves the lead to Contacted (the move hand-off exists). The same sheet from Notes › Log a call. Auto Fill from a chat stays the second way. The screenshot rule follows Q-02.
proposals.why: the call is the commonest moment on the move; three taps while it is fresh beats thirteen later.

proposals.title: The Move stage window: one step per screen, one Save & move
proposals.today: A full-screen form with a sideways rail (533px of tabs in 390, Won off-screen); New ticks a member only on its 44 checkbox; a completed log opens as a greyed form; Quote Sent / Won take a PDF only for the signed quote; Won’s split starts at 0% and Save refuses; On Hold is a sheet, Lost a centred card; feet 36–44.
proposals.proposed: Each step is one screen: a bar "Move to Met · step 3 of 5" (the rail goes), only that step’s fields in the order a finger fills them, one filled Save & move at 48; a refusal stays in the foot and nothing typed is lost (B-01’s data loss is fixed tonight). New: a member row is its label. Completed logs read as summary cards with Edit. Won as a checklist — the signed quote "OM-10008 · S$68,176 ✓" or Take a photo · Choose a file (Q-03), the signed contract the same, payments "10 · 30 · 30 · 30 — the studio’s usual", project type as chips, Create project. On Hold and Lost share one sheet (reason chips, the duration or the competitor, Save & move with Undo). At 1024 the window stays the centred modal.
proposals.why: moving a lead is the moment after a visit, often at the client’s table; one step per screen is one thing at a time.

proposals.title: The phone card says who to call now
proposals.today: The listing card is right in shape, but it cannot say who to call: Last contact and Next follow-up are listing columns that never reached it; the only date is the lead’s age at 12px; a new unseen lead has no mark on the phone; WhatsApp is not on the card; a refused stage move says why without a fix; a Lost card says nothing about why.
proposals.proposed: Keep the card; add Last ("Call · callback requested · Mon") and Next ("Call back · Thu 10:00", red when late) as one 14 line each, the new mark (the tablet’s primary band and a New chip), WhatsApp beside the number, three items on the info line. The stage sheet from a card puts the next move first; a locked row says why in the row with its fix (Assign). A "to call today" chip. Lost and Deleted views use the same card (the reason and the date; Restore on Deleted).
proposals.why: his benchmark keeps its shape; the two lines are what a designer between visits scrolls the list for.

proposals.title: The listing on a tablet: a column set, a frozen ⋮, a kanban that moves
proposals.today: At 768 the table shows Lead Name · Stage · part of Tasks of 1,544px; Edit and ⋮ are 850px of sideways scroll away; the kanban cannot move a lead on touch (drag gives way to the pan, no stage control, ⋮ holds Delete only).
proposals.proposed: The table core’s tablet default (REG-2564): Name · Stage · Last contact · Next follow-up · Members, Edit and ⋮ frozen at the right, the rest in Column settings remembered for the tablet (its handles and pins at 44). The kanban card carries the stage pill (the same sheet as the phone card); ⋮ holds Move to › and Delete. Numbers grouped everywhere; values at 14.
proposals.why: Quotes and Contracts made the same move this week; a lead’s tablet table should not be the exception.

proposals.title: The lead on a tablet: upright follows the phone, sideways two panes
proposals.today: The tablet is the desk squeezed: rail 52 + info column 300 + centre 320 + Create strip 72, so the cards are 272 wide at 768 portrait; the Create strip is nine unlabelled glyphs whose hit boxes are clipped to 28×44; Notes upright is master-detail at 280 + 268.
proposals.proposed: Held upright, the tablet gets the Lead screen (Q-01). Held sideways (1024): two panes — the hero, Next, Due now and the rows at the left (320–360), the open tab at the right; Log ▾ and the next move in the bar; Create in ⋮ (no glyph strip on touch). Notes upright opens a log full width.
proposals.why: the person beside the open tab is the landscape answer Quotes and Contracts gave.

proposals.title: A new lead is a name and a mobile; Edit details a short list
proposals.today: Create New Lead is a 9-field sheet that types at 14; its ✕ throws away what was typed without a word; Fill from a document opens a second card over the sheet; the duplicate dialog’s filled default creates the duplicate; Edit details is 17 fields in one 2.6-screen sheet.
proposals.proposed: Name and mobile on one screen (autocomplete name / tel, 16), "Paste the WhatsApp message to fill the rest" and Fill from a document in the same sheet, More details folded, Assign with the suggested member; one Add lead; ✕ asks before it discards; the duplicate dialog’s default is Open existing lead; the new lead opens on its Lead screen ready to call. Edit details is a short list (Contact · Property · Budget & source · People), each a screen.
proposals.why: a lead arrives in a hurry, usually from a message; three taps and nothing lost.

proposals.title: Imports on a phone fold what matched and say what won’t land
proposals.today: Mapping eleven columns that all matched is 5.9 screens of cards; the preview is the 12-column sheet and never flags the row with no name; the end says "4 of 5 imported" with no reason; merging one duplicate is 8.7 screens of Existing / New / Merged rows even when equal.
proposals.proposed: Mapping folds to "11 columns matched ✓ · Review" with only the unmatched as cards; the preview is a list of the leads with a red line on a row that won’t land ("No name — skipped"); the end names what was skipped and why; the merge shows only the fields that differ ("Phone: 9133 5520 → 9133 5521"), the rest under "13 the same"; the review queue’s card is the listing card.
proposals.why: a lead sheet arrives on WhatsApp too; reviewing it on a phone should be a list, not a spreadsheet.

proposals.title: Tasks on the move: whole names, due presets, a bulk bar of three
proposals.today: A task’s name is cut at 19 characters; Create New Task takes a title only (a due day is 8 more taps through a calendar whose controls are 24–32); the bulk bar needs 511px in 372 and pushes Delete off; the panel opens on Creator; on a tablet the table keeps the desk’s 1,395px in 570 (Meetings and Files the same).
proposals.proposed: A task row reads whole (two lines) with its due day as a chip and a 44 ring to tick it done; Add a task takes a title, a due preset (Tomorrow 10:00 · In 3 days · Next week · Pick a day) and a member in one row; the bulk bar is Done · Assign · ⋯; the panel opens on the task; tablet column sets for Tasks, Meetings and Files with ⋮ frozen. Module-wide: the rail’s /tasks and a project’s Tasks get the same.
proposals.why: "call back tomorrow at 10" is the commonest task on the move.

proposals.title: Files on a phone open on the camera
proposals.today: A site photo is seven taps (Files → New File → From Local Files → the OS sheet’s Take Photo …); "From Google Drive" answers Coming soon; inside a folder the toolbar splits into two rows; the viewer has no pinch and no swipe.
proposals.proposed: The Files screen’s first action is Take a photo (several in a row, into the open folder) with Choose files beside it; a folder keeps one toolbar row with the title its own line; the viewer pinches, swipes to the next file and keeps the chrome still.

proposals.title: Meetings, Questionnaire and Activity read first
proposals.today: A meeting card opens only from its 20px title; the meeting page is 3,037px with its Save scrolling away; the Questionnaire’s summary is the last card; Ask the client’s ticks are ragged on touch; Activity is a 4,643px flat log with ten "uploaded the file" rows in a row.
proposals.proposed: The whole meeting card opens it; the meeting page’s one Save to the lead in a sticky foot. Questionnaire: "4 to answer · 7 answered" on top with To answer / Answered chips; each Ask the client tick a full-width row. Activity grouped by day, repeats folded ("James uploaded 10 files").
proposals.why: read first: the count and the next thing before the list.

proposals.title: The scale 16 · 14 · 44 in every Leads surface
proposals.today: Card values and sentences at 12 (LEAD STAGES days, Last contact, Next follow-up, MY TASKS dates); file names and tags at 10; dates 12; sheet feet drawn 36; Sort radios 24; the search and the composer type at 14.
proposals.proposed: The rule Quotes and Contracts follow: text people read 16, secondary 14, never under 14 for a value, a name or a sentence; targets 44, feet 48; inputs at 16.
proposals.why: his rule after Quotes (responsive.md § On the move).

findingsTitle: What is wrong today, screen by screen
findingsIntro: Each finding names what was seen, where, and how bad. A finding the proposal resolves (or that was fixed tonight) says so and needs no pick. Severity: Blocker = can’t finish the job at that width · Major = hard, slow or error-prone · Minor = polish. The lanes’ full tables, measurements and shots are in the record folder.
findingsNote: most are covered by the proposal above; the rest are quick fixes you can pick

surfaces.title: The listing on a phone — the benchmark
surfaces.intro: You called the listing the part that is right, and it mostly is: one column of cards, the stage in reach, the number dials. What it cannot say yet is who to call now: the last contact and the next follow-up never reached the card.

findings.title: A new, unseen lead has no mark on the phone card
findings.what: Nothing on a card says a lead is new and unseen. The dock reads "Leads (1 new)" and the tablet paints Chloe Tan's 4px primary band; her phone card is identical to the other 30. The only way to find what is new is the dock badge's `?scope=unseen` — and the moment that matters most on the move is the new enquiry (the studio's own tip on Return Lead: "Contact within 2 hours").
findings.absorbedNote: the new mark on the phone card

findings.title: The Maison AI button covers the card’s stage pill
findings.what: The FAB sits on the stage pill. Whenever a card's foot crosses y 644–692 with the button shown (at rest, and every time the chrome returns on a scroll up) the 48px FAB (x 326–374) covers the right 32px of the pill (x 230–358); `elementFromPoint` on the pill's chevron returns the FAB — the tap opens Maison AI instead of the stage sheet.
findings.fix: Swap the card's foot (stage pill left, members right — the pill is the press, the avatars are not), or let the FAB step out of the listing at ≤767 as it steps out of a tablet section screen (REG-2587), its three suggestions behind the header ⋮ ("Ask Maison AI").

findings.title: A card cannot say who to call now
findings.what: A card cannot say who to call now. Last contact (REG-600) and Next follow-up (REG-608) are listing columns that never reached the card; the task box shows the first task's title + "OVERDUE" but not its date; the only date is the lead's created age at 12px ("6d ago", "30 Aug ’26"). Farah Ahmad reads "Follow up on WhatsApp · OVERDUE · +2" — overdue since when, and when did we last speak?
findings.absorbedNote: last contact and next follow-up on the card

findings.title: The card’s info line wraps after a dangling separator
findings.what: The line carries four items where the canvas drew three ("· 6 days in New", UX audit L3), so 18 of 31 cards wrap and the break lands after a dangling separator ("Hangout ·" / "6 days in New"); cards alternate 173 / 197 tall.
findings.absorbedNote: three items on the info line

findings.title: WhatsApp is not on the card; the name and number boxes overlap
findings.what: The number dials (tel:, UX audit L11) but WhatsApp — Singapore's main channel, on the identity block of the lead's page — is not on the card. The name row's 44 box and the number's 44 box overlap by ~18px: the head measures 38 tall, the number 32–36, so a tap just under the name dials.
findings.absorbedNote: Call and WhatsApp beside the name

findings.title: A refused move from a card says why but offers no fix
findings.what: A refused move says why only after the tap, in a snackbar, with no way to fix it. Olivia Martinez (no member) → Contacted is grey; tapping it raises "Assign a member first" over the sheet — no Assign in it. Finishing the job costs 6 taps: close · the card's Assign · tick · Assign · the pill again · Contacted. Met / Quote Sent / Won are grey with no word until each is tapped.
findings.absorbedNote: a locked row says why with its fix

findings.title: The card’s pill says where the lead is, not the next move
findings.what: The card's biggest control is labelled with where the lead IS ("New ▾") and opens a 7-row list where 3–4 rows are off; the lead's page offers the same move as one filled "Move to Contacted". The common move from the listing is two taps and a read.
findings.absorbedNote: the sheet puts the next move first

findings.title: The Assign sheet from a card never names the lead
findings.what: Titled "Assign Member" and never names the lead, while the stage and tasks sheets from the same card do ("Chloe Tan · 9331 8842 · Current stage: New"); the card is under the scrim, so nothing confirms whose lead is being assigned. Role captions 12.
findings.absorbedNote: every sheet from a card names the lead

findings.title: Add Task from a card takes no due date
findings.what: Adds a task with no due date: one field + Cancel / Save. "Call back tomorrow at 10" — the commonest task on the move — needs card → lead → Tasks → task panel. The sheet's own words are 12 ("OPEN TASKS · 0", the subject line, "Follow-up · Mon, 26 Oct ’26 · 10:00 AM"); the field types at 14.
findings.absorbedNote: Add a task with a due preset

findings.title: Two search glasses, two scopes; the field types at 14
findings.what: Two magnifiers 128px apart with two scopes: the top bar's opens ⌘K (the studio), the toolbar's filters this list. Opened, the field types at 14 (16 only inside the iOS `@supports` rule), and its clear ✕ is a 20×20 target.
findings.absorbedNote: one search per screen, typing at 16

findings.title: Filters is the desktop’s two-pane modal inside a sheet
findings.what: The desktop's two-pane modal in a sheet (rail 156 + pane 234). Its height follows the tab — Sort 453, Date 493, Members 743 — so the head jumps 290px under the thumb; Quick filters repeats the pill's To do scopes (Overdue follow-ups · Unassigned · Unseen) as checkboxes; Done never says what the live filters leave, and the list is behind the sheet.
findings.fix: The sheet holds its tallest height; Done reads "Show 9 leads"; the To do scopes live on the pill only; (later) one scrolling sheet of sections on the house `Chips`, as Quotes A-21 proposed.

findings.title: Deleted Leads is still an 8-column table on a phone
findings.what: Still the 8-column table on a phone (1,316 wide in 356): Restore and Delete Forever sit ~960px to the right; the head sort buttons are 16-tall targets; Empty Trash — the destructive one — is an outlined button beside ✕ at the top right. REG-378 gave Deleted Files the list treatment; Deleted Leads never got it.
findings.absorbedNote: Deleted Leads as the card with Restore

findings.title: A Lost card says nothing about why or when
findings.what: A Lost card says nothing about why or when (the reason, the competitor, the expected restart — REG-607 / REG-640); it still shows its task in red ("Respond to Qanvast team · OVERDUE") though Overdue follow-ups leaves Lost out; its pill opens the 7-row sheet where resuming is "New ✓".
findings.absorbedNote: a Lost card says why and when

surfaces.title: The listing on a tablet
surfaces.intro: A touch tablet opens the desktop table and a kanban that cannot move a lead.

findings.title: The tablet table shows three of eight columns
findings.what: Three columns on the first screen. At 768 the 642 frame holds Lead Name 240 · Stage 146 · Tasks (256 of 321) of a 1,544 grid (2.4 screens); Members starts at x 800, Budget at 1,092. At 1024 the frame is 898 and Source is cut mid-word. Rows stand 105 (name 12+24+12, the phone row 44, cell 8+8): 7 leads a screen. The listing still reads `useColumnPrefs('leads', …)`, not the tablet default Quotes added.
findings.absorbedNote: the tablet column set

findings.title: Edit and ⋮ sit 850px of sideways scroll away on a tablet
findings.what: Edit + ⋮ are 850px (768) / 617px (1024) of sideways scroll away (x 1,515 / 1,585 in frames ending at 735 / 991). The ⋮ there holds one row, Delete. Nothing on the first screen says a row has actions; the name is the only way in.
findings.absorbedNote: Edit and ⋮ frozen at the right

findings.title: The tablet’s phone numbers and card dates read 12
findings.what: The phone under each name is 12 (body/s) in the table, the kanban card's "Updated 6d ago" 12, the review queue's info line 12 and status tag 10.
findings.absorbedNote: 14 on a tablet

findings.title: The kanban cannot move a lead on a touch tablet
findings.what: The board cannot move a lead. Drag gives way to the pan on touch (REG-379), the card has no stage control, and its ⋮ holds Delete only — the stage board is read-only on an iPad. Columns are 416 / 422 wide in 644 / 898 frames (1.5 / 2.1 visible) with no snap.
findings.absorbedNote: a stage control on the kanban card

findings.title: Phone numbers print ungrouped on the kanban and the review queue
findings.what: The kanban card prints "96652018" and the review queue "91335520" where the table and the phone card read "9665 2018".
findings.absorbedNote: numbers grouped everywhere

findings.title: Column settings’ handles and pins are 24px on a tablet
findings.what: Drag handles and pins are 24×24 targets on a touch tablet (measured 24×24, no growth), and order changes only by dragging a 24px handle. Module-wide: every list's drawer.
findings.absorbedNote: Column settings at 44 on touch

surfaces.measure: At 768 the 642 frame holds Lead Name 240 · Stage 146 · Tasks of a 1,544 grid; Edit and ⋮ at x 1,515.

surfaces.title: A new lead and the imports
surfaces.intro: How a lead arrives on a phone: typed, pasted from a message, or imported. The form loses what was typed on a stray ✕; the import is the desktop wizard in a sheet.

findings.title: ✕ on Create New Lead throws away what was typed
findings.what: ✕ throws away what was typed: with a name typed — or with the nine fields a document just filled — the close discards without a word. The import wizard asks ("Are you sure you want to close?"); this form, the one filled during a call, doesn't. (The scrim tap does not close — good.)
findings.absorbedNote: ✕ asks before it discards

findings.title: The lead form types at 14 with no name / phone autocomplete
findings.what: Every input types at 14 (the 16 rule is iOS-only, so Android and an iPad reading desktop get 14); the name has no `autocapitalize="words"` / `autocomplete="name"`, the phone no `autocomplete="tel"`; the helper "Client project address." and the fill summary are 12. Additional info opens to 1,688px of fields in a 602 body (2.8 screens) in one run.
findings.absorbedNote: 16 and autocomplete

findings.title: Fill from a document opens a second card over the sheet
findings.what: On a phone it reads "Drop in the document or browse" in a 342 centred card over the sheet (two scrims), Cancel + Upload under a dropzone that is itself the button; it takes PDF / XLSX / CSV / TXT but not what arrives on a phone — a WhatsApp message or a screenshot.
findings.absorbedNote: paste a message or a document in the same sheet

findings.title: The duplicate dialog’s default creates the duplicate
findings.what: "Create anyway" is the filled button, "Open existing lead" the outlined one: the one-thumb default makes the duplicate. The help line is 12.
findings.absorbedNote: the default opens the existing lead

findings.title: The import toast shows a CSV badge for every file
findings.what: The upload toast draws a CSV badge for every file — `/figma-assets/file-csv.svg` is hard-coded, so an XLSX (and a PDF) shows "CSV" — and on a phone it covers the success card above the foot. Half of the first screen is tips and a template download a phone can't edit.
findings.fix: The badge from the extension (the Files tab's kind icons); ≤767 the toast becomes the dropzone's own row; tips fold under "How to prepare the file".

findings.title: Mapping eleven matched columns takes 5.9 screens
findings.what: Eleven columns, all auto-matched, still cost 2,739px of mapping cards in a 468 body (5.9 screens — name, AUTO-MATCHED, three samples and a select each) before Next.
findings.absorbedNote: matched columns fold to one line

findings.title: The import preview never flags the row that won’t land
findings.what: The preview is the 12-column sheet (2,050px wide in 356 / 622) and says nothing about what won't land: row 5 has no name and is dropped — step 4 says "4 of 5 records imported successfully" with no reason — and Gerald Tan (an existing lead's phone) isn't flagged until the review queue. The routing dialog still asks about "these 5 leads".
findings.absorbedNote: the preview says what won’t land and why

findings.title: Merging one duplicate takes 8.7 screens
findings.what: Merging one duplicate at 390 is 3,937px of scroll in a 450 window: each of 15 fields stacks Existing / New / Merged rows even when both sides are "—" or equal; only Phone differs (⚠). The source chips, the switch and Approve All Clean (190px) stay above the merge; the three-button foot + note takes 145. At 768 the New column is cut under the frozen Merged result ("Ge…", "identic…", "120…") — the values being merged are hidden until a sideways pan.
findings.absorbedNote: the merge shows only what differs

findings.title: The review queue’s cards print 10–12px; Approve All is a green button
findings.what: Queue cards print the phone ungrouped, the info line at 12, the status tag at 10; "Approve All Clean (16)" — a green filled button, not the house primary — adds 16 leads in one tap and answers with a plain snackbar, no Undo.
findings.absorbedNote: the queue card is the listing card

findings.title: Import History reads “4 of 5imported”
findings.what: The counts read "4 of 5imported", "13 of 14imported", "233 of 243imported": the ≤767 `::after { content: ' imported' }` has no `white-space: pre`, so its leading space collapses (REG-390 gave the other two separators `pre`, not this one).

findings.title: Return Lead runs the whole form on an expired window
findings.what: One clean column, but on an expired window ("Return period expired (30 days) · 0 of 2 returns used") the reason, Attach Files and a filled Next → Confirm still run the whole form with nothing saying what an expired return becomes; the tips card (four lines at 12) sits between the fields and the foot.
findings.fix: One sentence first: "The 30 days are over — Qanvast decides; it goes as a late return"; tips folded, at 14.

surfaces.measure: Mapping 11 matched columns: 2,739px (5.9 screens). Merging one duplicate: 3,937px (8.7 screens).

surfaces.title: The lead’s page
surfaces.intro: A lead is a person and a position, not a document. Today the phone page is the desktop’s three columns stacked: 2.9–3.8 screens, the primary scrolls away, Call is a 70×20 link.

findings.title: Call, Copy and WhatsApp are the page’s smallest targets
findings.what: The page's two most-used on-site actions are its smallest targets: the tel: number 70×20, Copy 24×24 and WhatsApp 24×24, 8 px apart; email 79×20, Copy email 24×24. **This is a decision** (REG-365: the owner kept the block's 8 px rhythm "below REG-273's 44 floor"). It doesn't serve someone holding the phone in one hand at a client's door.
findings.absorbedNote: Call and WhatsApp as 44 buttons in the hero

findings.title: The one primary scrolls away on a 3-screen page

surfaces.title: The Move stage window and the moments
surfaces.intro: The moments a designer does on site in one hand: log the call, move after the visit, win with the signed papers. One of them lost data — fixed tonight.

findings.title: An unowned lead’s first log was lost on Save — fixed tonight
findings.what: On a lead nobody owns, "Move to Contacted" opens the window **at Contacted** (`stageIntent` returns `wizard` for the next stage without the owner gate that `blockedReason` and the stage menu apply). I filled the whole log (Call · date · outcome · a screenshot), pressed Save → Suggested tasks → "Move without tasks": the server refused ("Couldn’t move the lead — assign a member first"), **the window closed and the log was gone** — 0 `lead_notes`, 0 `stage_logs`; the screenshot stayed in Files, once per attempt (two copies after two tries). Every lead an Owner or Admin adds lands like this (only a Designer self-assigns, REG-609).
findings.absorbedNote: fixed tonight as REG-2655 — every forward stage move now asks the owner rule first, and the lead page’s refusal offers Assign

findings.title: The New step ticks a member only on its checkbox
findings.what: Only the 44×44 checkbox at the right edge ticks a member; the rest of the 358×64 row — avatar, name, role — does nothing (a tap on "Dane" left it unticked). The foot reads "Save changes" while the lead is still in New, and Save closes the window ("Members updated") instead of carrying on: you press "Move to Contacted" a second time. Nothing in the Contacted step says New still needs someone (the rail's empty circle is the only sign).
findings.absorbedNote: a member row is its label

findings.title: A completed log opens as a greyed form
findings.what: A completed log opens as the **form, greyed** — chips, fields and the attachment at disabled contrast, with Edit in the card head and **Cancel** alone in the foot. You can't read the call back at a glance: the value is inside a disabled input.
findings.absorbedNote: a completed log is a summary card with Edit

findings.title: Logging a first call takes 13 taps and a screenshot
findings.what: Thirteen taps, and a screenshot is mandatory: Call chip (1) · Date & Time (3: the sheet, today, Done — the field opens empty; `defaultNow` only supplies the time once a day is picked) · Outcome (2, an anchored list that opens upward over the chips, not a sheet) · Attach (an "Attach files" sheet whose words are "Drop your file or browse", then the OS picker, then "Attach 1 File" at 36 tall) · Save · Suggested tasks › Save. The window demands the screenshot (REG-543 kept it) **but the same contact log on Notes doesn't** ("Attach screenshots of your call attempts" has no `*` there) — one log, two rules. Auto Fill from an exported chat is fast (5 taps, it filled channel, time, outcome and the next meeting), but only if a file exists.
findings.absorbedNote: three taps after a call

findings.title: A signed quote at Won cannot be a photo
findings.what: Both quote uploads take PDF only (`accept=".pdf"`). A photo of a signed paper quote is refused with "Choose a PDF — the quote is kept as one", while the **signed contract on the same Won screen** offers Take a photo · Choose a file (C4 P-12).
findings.absorbedNote: Take a photo for the signed quote

findings.title: Won’s payment split starts at 0% and Save refuses
findings.what: An uploaded quote zeroes the split (REG-149, a decision). On the phone that means four 48×42 % boxes at 14 px, typed one by one. Save is refused with "Milestones must add up to 100%" until you find **Reset to default**. The "0%" badge is 10 px, and "Total S$70,500" shows while 0 % is assigned.
findings.absorbedNote: the studio’s usual split

findings.title: On Hold is a sheet, Lost a centred card
findings.what: On Hold is a bottom sheet titled "Put on hold"; Lost is a centred card titled "Move stage". Both carry a reason select and fields (P-10 changed only On Hold).
findings.absorbedNote: On Hold and Lost share one sheet

findings.title: A refusal’s snackbar sits on the On Hold sheet’s chips
findings.what: A stage-menu refusal's snackbar ("Assign a member first") stayed on screen across the Duration chips of the On Hold sheet that opened next (snackbar y 711–759 over chips 675–719): the chips' effective box dropped to 36. The chips' words are 12 px.
findings.fix: `Dialog`'s phone sheet lifts `--snackbar-bottom` the way `Sheet` does (`useSheetFootLift`); a refusal's snackbar is dismissed when the next surface opens. Chip text 14.

findings.title: Two snackbars with two Undos stack
findings.what: Hold then Resume left two snackbars showing at once, each with its own Undo ("Laneb Beta is on hold · Undo" over "Moved to New · Undo"): 112 px over the page, and the older Undo now undoes a hold that is already over.
findings.fix: The stage moves share one snackbar `key`, so the newest replaces the last.

findings.what: Foot "Cancel / Attach 1 File" 36 tall; File Type 36; sort 36×36; the words are the desk's ("Drop your file or browse · Supports: JPEG, PNG, PDF"); no camera.

findings.title: The window’s and its dialogs’ feet are 36–44
findings.what: The Move stage foot is Cancel / Save at 44, right-aligned. The nested Auto Fill and Suggested tasks cards use 36-tall buttons ("Move without tasks" 164×36). The Auto Fill helper is 12 px.

surfaces.title: Tasks (the lead’s, the rail’s and a project’s)
surfaces.intro: The Tasks tab shares its component with the rail’s /tasks and a project’s Tasks: every finding here is module-wide.

findings.title: The Tasks toolbar’s tap areas are shifted 22–24px left
findings.what: **Hit boxes are shifted 22–24px left of the glyphs.** `.touchTarget::after { inset: -4px }` on top of the house IconButton's `translate(-50%,-50%)` box. At 390: Filters drawn 290–326 hits 265–312, so its right 14px open **More options**; Search drawn 242–278 hits 238–264 (27 wide). Same at 768 (Column settings drawn 580–616 hits 555–602) and on /tasks. Meetings: New Meeting hits 217–277 and steals Briefs' right half (Briefs hits 165–216 of 168–230); Search 27 wide; More options takes Search's right half. The design lint misses it: its `icon-button-overlay` rule only matches `button::after`.
findings.fix: Delete the three overrides (`tasks-toolbar.module.css`, `task-panel.module.css` `.touchTarget::after`, `meetings-toolbar.module.css` `.menuWrap > button::after`); widen the lint to any `::after` with `inset` on a class passed to `IconButton`.

findings.title: A task’s checkbox is hittable in a 24px band
findings.what: The row checkbox's 44 box is hittable only 24–26px tall on the lead's tab (the title cell paints over its top 20px). On the rail's **/tasks** the box's drawn centre is dead: a real tap at (36, 343) hit `tasks-table cell` and selected nothing. The comment chip ("2") is 36×24 — its `::after` sits under the next cell. Module-wide (one `tasks-table`).
findings.fix: Raise `.cell.colSel` and the chip above the cells (`z-index`) — or, as the Quotes card did, drop the checkbox on a phone and select by long press (`use-long-press.ts`).

findings.what: One selected task: Assign · Mark as completed · Save as Template · Duplicate · Delete · ✕ need 511px in a 372 bar. Duplicate is cut, **Delete and Clear selection are off the right edge**, with no sign the bar scrolls. REG-358 meant the scroll for the 320 floor only.

findings.title: A task’s name is cut at 19 characters
findings.what: A task's name is cut at ~19 characters at 14px ("Book the showroom v…", "Send the revis…"); at 320, 10 characters, and the due date runs under the ⋮. The member cell wraps to a **third line that starts at x 28, under the checkbox**, while the title starts at x 104: 129px per task, 5 tasks = 645px. The canvas (2b) draws two lines.

questionsIntro: Where the proposal has more than one good answer. My recommendation is marked.

questions.title: Does a tablet in portrait (768) get the phone model, as Quotes and Contracts do?
opts: The phone model with room: the Lead screen, tabs as screens, one step per screen
The desktop page with the type and target fixes
Phone model up to 1024 in portrait; two panes only sideways

questions.title: Is a contact log’s screenshot mandatory?
opts: Optional in both places, with Take a photo offered first — the log is what matters on the move (the Move stage window asks for it today, Notes does not)
Mandatory in both, as the window does today (REG-543)
Mandatory in the window only, as today

questions.title: May a signed quote be a photo at Quote Sent and Won?
opts: Yes — kept as the copy, the amount typed, as the signed contract already is (Contracts’ Q-04)
No — a quote stays a PDF

questions.title: The stage row on every tab (your REG-370): on a phone’s tab screens too?
opts: Not on a phone’s tab screens — the next move is one Back away in the Lead screen’s foot; tablets and the desk keep it
Keep it on every tab at every width, as REG-370 decided
Keep it on a phone as a one-line chip in the tab’s bar

questions.title: The card’s stage control on the listing
opts: Keep the pill (where the lead is) — its sheet puts the next move first and says why a locked row is locked, with its fix
Show the next move on the card ("Move to Contacted") with the pill behind ⋮
No stage control on the card; move from the lead

questions.title: After a call from the app, how does the log come up?
opts: A one-line prompt on the Lead screen when you come back — "Log the call with Farah · Log" — never a sheet that opens by itself
The log sheet opens by itself when you come back
Nothing automatic: Log ▾ in the foot

questions.title: The Lead screen’s filled button
opts: The next move, as the header’s primary today (Move to Met · Convert to Project · Resume at …), with Log ▾ beside it; the Next line names the job
The state’s capture (Log a contact · Log the meeting · Create quote), with the move behind Stage ▾

questions.title: After Leads, which module next?
opts: Projects — the schedule, updates, money and choices on site (the module most used outside the office)
Tasks and Tickets in the rail
Company, Settings and the price book
